target.title: Rework Android gateway onboarding setup
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Android first-run gateway setup was hard to follow: the setup-code path was not clearly the recommended authenticated path, nearby discovery looked like a primary pairing method even though it only helps with endpoints, and the transition through connecting, node approval, and connected states gave users little guidance. ## Why This Change Was Made This reworks Android onboarding around the current product truth: generating a setup code with `openclaw qr` is the golden path because it carries bootstrap auth, nearby gateway discovery can only assist with an endpoint, and manual setup is a fallback. It also gives node approval and connection progress dedicated UI states so users know what is happening after a QR scan or setup-code entry. ## User Impact - New Android users see a dark-mode welcome screen, a clearer gateway connection choice screen, and a setup walkthrough before scanning. - The QR scanner opens inline in a square camera tile, with close, gallery, and setup-code fallback controls available from the same screen. - Manual setup stays available as a fallback, with local nearby endpoint data used as prefill when available instead of as a separate primary action. - Pairing progress now explains gateway check, secure session creation, and node approval waiting states; successful pairing lands on a connected screen before continuing. - Node approval is a dedicated follow-up screen with the two gateway commands users need, and the app only advances after a fresh approval check sees the gateway/node ready state. - Camera permission for QR scanning remains separate from granting OpenClaw camera tool access. ## What Changed - Android onboarding UI: replaces the old gateway pairing flow with welcome, connect gateway, setup gateway, inline scanner, setup-code, manual, progress, approval, error, and connected states. - Navigation behavior: centralizes expected back transitions for the onboarding subflow and covers them with logic tests. - Android gateway state: persists gateway auth/session details, distinguishes setup progress from node approval, preserves existing operator device-token scopes on reconnect, and removes the inactive sign-out dead end from the paired shell path. - Bootstrap handoff: updates the device bootstrap contract/tests/docs for bounded operator handoff scopes used after mobile pairing. - Merge refresh: rebased the proof against current `main`; `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/MainViewModel.kt` is branch churn only and has no current net behavior change. ## Screenshots Captured from the `OpenClaw_Pixel_8_API_35` Android emulator at 1080x2400. Full phone viewport is used because the changed header/back controls, vertical centering, scanner tile, and bottom actions are part of the proof. | Screenshot | Claim Proved | State | Viewport | Crop Choice | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | Welcome uses the dark-mode Android shell with concise setup expectations and one bottom CTA. | Fresh install / welcome | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Gateway choice screen makes setup code primary and manual setup secondary without promoting nearby discovery as pairing. | Connect Gateway | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Setup walkthrough explains starting the gateway and generating a setup code before scanner actions. | Setup Gateway instructions | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | QR camera opens inline in the scanner square and keeps close/gallery/setup-code controls in context. | QR scanner active | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Scanner tile has a readable camera-unavailable state with the same fallback actions. | QR scanner with no emulator camera | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Setup-code entry is reachable as a focused fallback instead of a confusing scanner input box. | Enter setup code | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Invalid setup code feedback is prominent and recoverable. | Invalid setup-code error | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Manual setup remains a fallback with URL/token fields and clear pairing action. | Manual setup | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Connection progress is contained inside the main setup box with explicit current work instead of a silent spinner. | Connecting progress | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Later pairing progress/approval state keeps the user in setup with visible next-step progress. | Approval/progress state | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | ## Verification Reviewer-checkable behavior: - Android onboarding logic tests cover the golden setup-code path, back destinations, manual fallback, pairing progress, node approval stop/check/continue behavior, permission reapproval routing, and QR/setup-code error states. - Gateway/node tests cover setup-code bootstrap auth, stored operator device-token scope preservation, split node-list approval parsing, and node approval refresh triggers. - Native i18n inventory was regenerated from source after the merge conflict resolution. Automated/local checks: - `cd apps/android && ANDROID_HOME=/Users/jmerhi/Library/Android/sdk ANDROID_SDK_ROOT=/Users/jmerhi/Library/Android/sdk GRADLE_USER_HOME=/tmp/openclaw-gradle-user-home ./gradlew :app:compilePlayDebugKotlin :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.GatewayBootstrapAuthTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.GatewayNodeApprovalStateTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.OnboardingFlowLogicTest --no-daemon` passed. - `node --import tsx scripts/native-app-i18n.ts sync --write` regenerated `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`. - `node --import tsx scripts/native-app-i18n.ts check` passed with `changed=false`. - `git diff --check` and `git diff --cached --check` passed before the merge-resolution commit. - Fresh CI is expected to rerun on pushed head `f400841931bd`.
